blocks.note: Form the basic werden-passive by promoting the accusative object and supplying the participle.
Select an appropriate process-passive tense from the time and discourse context.
Build passive infinitive clusters under modal verbs while preserving the original tense.
Keep dative and prepositional objects unchanged, form impersonal passives, and reject lexically impossible passives.
Produce subjectless passives from activities and control first-position es.
Choose werden for a process and sein for a resulting or continuing state.
Contrast ordinary passive clauses with reflexive alternatives expressing results and characteristic behavior.
Recast modal passives with sein or bleiben plus zu, sich lassen, es gibt, and gehören.
Compress passive possibility into adjectives in -bar, -lich, and -fähig.
Integrate passive formation, valency limits, process-state distinctions, and idiomatic alternatives in translation.
